title: Wanted Posters
text: “This is a town where heavy taxation makes coming and going quite difficult, but will that be alright, I wonder?”

“Ah, is that so? Well, circuses tend to get treated pretty leniently around here, so it should be fine. Apparently the nobility here also have their hands in the slave trade. We’ve even got an invitation from a slave merchant.”

Oh ho, so while the toll for regular trading caravans was steep, circuses and slave dealings get passed through cheaply. It seemed that Father’s circus was starting to make waves in the entertainment world too, one way or another.
“Imiya-chan, why don’t you hide in the wagon for a bit now?”
“Y-yes…”

Father gave instructions to Mole, who had been sitting on his lap. This was apparently a matter of mental care—Father engaging in a bit of skinship. It hadn’t been long yet, but between the treatment of her injuries and the delicious meals, she seemed to be gradually regaining some vitality. Getting Big Sister, Older Sister, and even Panda’s family home to register as places safe enough to sleep in was apparently important. After all, Mole had suffered mental damage from failing to save someone. We were nearly at the plot of land where the circus tent would be set up. The townsfolk seemed to be eyeing us with curiosity, as though wondering if a circus was about to open. But it seemed one of the monster merchant’s subordinates had come to report something to Father. Hmm… now that I thought of it, if Itsuki had been active without incident, it was about time for him to go sticking his nose into some incident involving Riska being captured by the local nobility.
“Ah, is that so? Hmm… so what should we do, then?”
“Woof? What’s wrong?”
“Is something the matter, Iwatani-sama?”
“Not setting up?”
The slaves, Wolf included, had gathered around Father. So I decided to join the circle as well.
“What is it?”
Ren also climbed down from the wagon, apparently wanting to hear too. Éclair, Panda, and Elephant all seemed to be waiting for instructions as well.

“Ah, everyone. Um… well… it seems there was some kind of incident here, and this town is really on edge about demi-humans and beastmen right now. Looks like holding the circus is going to be difficult.”
“An incident?”

“Yeah. A few days ago, apparently the local lord was killed by a beastman, so not only is running a circus with demi-humans and beastmen dangerous, but in the wake of the incident the slave merchants are being extra strict about enforcing slave crests.”

Supposedly the sale of slaves was accelerating because of it, making it a decent time to buy cheap. Oh? This was slightly off from the timing when Itsuki would normally deal with this lord—so the lord here had been killed instead. This was an event that hadn’t occurred in any previous loop.
“The lord was murdered… what a dangerous story.”
“…Things have escalated to the point where such incidents occur?”
Éclair narrowed her eyes and murmured, while Crocodile Guy let out a deep sigh.
“Various factors could be imagined, but it was likely bound to happen sooner or later.”
“And on top of that, apparently a noble’s daughter who’d come from a neighboring territory for service has gone missing too, causing quite a stir.”
“Woof, so who’s the culprit? I heard it was a beastman.”
“Apparently the noble who was the victim was a terrible person… it seems it’s known he purchased several slaves for the purpose of abuse.”
“In that case, breaking through a slave crest to kill one’s master… that would take some serious grudge to pull off.”
“We don’t know for certain it was a slave, do we? Could’ve been someone who broke in to save a companion.”
There were demi-humans from Éclair’s own territory living in Melromarc, after all. But something like this had never happened before. What could be the cause, I wondered?

Anyway, it seemed wanted posters listing the slaves the lord had supposedly purchased, along with other suspicious individuals, were being circulated around town. Every single one looked like the face of some vicious criminal. But the wanted posters in this country tended to bear images that were, more often than not, far from anything resembling actual identification. Even when Father had been wanted, there were plenty of cases where it was hard to tell if the picture was even him. The same went for Filo-tan and Big Sister. There had even been one occasion where a hideously ugly raccoon-like beastman drawing was put up, supposedly depicting Big Sister. Years later, Father had kept one of those wanted posters labeled as Big Sister, and showed it to her saying, “Ah, nostalgic. To think this is supposed to be Raphtalia,” only for Big Sister to demand to know why on earth he still had it. His reasoning, apparently, was that he thought it had a certain artistic charm worth preserving. Anyway, there were the posted sketches of the suspected culprits.

Several demi-humans were drawn among them. There was also one strange figure who might’ve been a hamster, a squirrel, or a flying squirrel—impossible to tell—alongside another odd one that could’ve been a mole or a naked mole rat, equally indeterminate. There was also a call for information. This one was, quite plainly, Riska. Father took the paper and I read along with him.
“Motoyasu-kun, know anything about this?”
“I do not, indeed. If anything, nothing like this has ever happened before.”
“Hmm, so then, could our actions this time around—the circus, or maybe Rafumi-chan—be the cause?”

Let’s see, let’s see… The noble had apparently died in the underground dungeon of his mansion, seemingly impaled all over his body by someone while being tortured to death. There were countless stab wounds, and on top of that, burn marks from cursed flames… this could only be the work of some kind of curse magic. If it were Rival, she could absolutely pull off such a gruesome killing. Could it be that she had already crossed over into this world and was secretly at work somewhere? Knowing her, it wouldn’t be strange at all for her to have done exactly that.
“Sounds like it was a pretty gruesome scene. Is there a race capable of killing someone like this?”
“It looks like a combination of physical methods and magical ones.”
“Woof… impaling the entire body, then cursing and burning it… that’s not a method of killing you see much of, even in Siltvelt.”
“What kind of grudge would drive someone to that, hmm? Elmelo, you know anything?”
“…It’s not that I don’t know of people in Siltvelt well-versed in curse magic, but this one, I can’t say.”
Apparently Panda had asked Elephant because there were somewhat more of that kind of faction among the rats under Elephant’s command.
“Sounds like something Luna would know about. She uses dark magic, doesn’t she?”
“Hnn?”
Luna-chan was indeed a practitioner of dark magic, but no, this wasn’t her doing.
“No… this is exactly the kind of thing Rafumi could pull off! That girl’s been running around doing whatever she pleases without permission!”
“Don’t go pinning your own crimes on me. As if I’d do something so pointless. The only ones Rafumi punishes are those who treat chocolate as a mere plaything.”
She’d appeared out of nowhere to deny my deduction.
“So the whole body was impaled, then burned with cursed flames until dead, was it…”

For a moment, I recalled the skills and reflection effects from when Father used to wield the Curse Shield. Iron Maiden, was it? And also Dark Curse Burning? Either of those two skills could accomplish this, but since Father could no longer use the Curse Shield, it wasn’t something he could’ve carried out.
“If it wasn’t a single culprit but multiple, it’s conceivable. Or else…”
At that point, the fluffy Rabbit Guy was staring right at me.
“What is it? I have no reason to kill someone like this in a place like this, do I? If I were to kill him, I’d turn him to light without leaving so much as a speck of dust behind.”

This particular noble was one Itsuki would’ve dealt with and arrested if left alone anyway. There was no need for me to step in personally. Well, if he’d been abusing a Filolial-sama, I would have killed him mercilessly, mind you.
“Either way, this isn’t a great place to be, so let’s skip the circus here and just move on, doing our slave purchasing along the way instead. Sounds like they’re selling them off cheap.”
“…This may well have pushed relations between Melromarc and Siltvelt even further apart.”

Éclair’s single remark lingered heavily over the scene. There was no cheerful “let’s brighten this place up with a circus!” to be had here. After all, since Father’s circus had so many demi-humans and beastmen, this wasn’t the sort of situation where we could go spreading cheerful news. It seemed the Three Heroes Church faction in town was loudly proclaiming the exclusion of demi-humans. At this rate, Itsuki might catch wind of the bad rumors and come charging in. After all, he still seemed to be active. I had no idea how exactly he was operating, though—since Itsuki liked to disguise himself, he might well be going around in a robe, claiming to be a hero using nothing but a bow.
“I wonder what’s become of the successor noble set to govern this town.”
“Éclair, this is Melromarc, remember?”
“…It’s infuriating that there’s nothing I can say. All we can do is pray for the Queen’s swift return.”
“…If Eclair-san or Shion were to set foot in this town, it’d likely stir up trouble. I do hope you’ll bear with it here.”

According to Father’s read on things, it seemed likely that demi-humans and beastmen were being killed and put on display as a warning to others. And so, when it came to purchasing, Father decided to enlist the cooperation of the monster merchant’s subordinates and Older Sister, keeping things simple—taking only a cursory look at the slaves in this town and refraining from buying anyone who wasn’t originally a villager. And so the circus caravan hurried onward toward its next destination.
Happy New Year, everyone. Thank you for your continued support this year as well.
